title: The recursion theorem: programs that use their own indices

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 72–76 (§§3.4–3.5.1, fixed points and elementary self-reference); version 2007-01-09

summary: Construct programs whose behavior depends on their own indices, and distinguish a fixed point of computed behavior from an unchanged program number.
abstract: Can a program return its own numerical index without being given that index as input? The recursion theorem shows how to build one, and more generally how a program can use its own index in any partial recursive computation. The construction inserts a fixed input into program text twice, using the effective parameter theorem. It also proves that every total computable transformation of program indices preserves the behavior of at least one program. This is equality of computed partial functions: the original and transformed indices can be different numbers. Concrete examples show both total self-referential behavior and a case in which the required equality forces divergence.
